title: From Hardware to Durable Data
description: A systems learning path through computer architecture, operating systems, and databases. Explain where a guarantee comes from, test where it fails, and defend the evidence.
scope: This is an advanced self-study path, not a beginner programming course, degree, accreditation, or promise of employment. Architecture precedes OS here because its machine model supports kernel reasoning; databases then make persistence and concurrency visible at the application boundary. The courses can also be studied independently with their stated prerequisites.

preparation.title: C and data structures
preparation.description: Pointers, object lifetime, allocation failure, linked structures, arrays, hashing, trees, and cost analysis. MIT 6.087 assumes prior programming and includes C exercises; its historical Athena environment is not provided by OCW.

preparation.title: Discrete mathematics
preparation.description: Sets, relations, predicates, induction, invariants, counting, and probability. Use the open textbook and problems to close specific gaps.

preparation.title: Development tools
preparation.description: A shell, Git, a compiler, a debugger, and reproducible commands. The Missing Semester provides independent tool practice; OS kernel labs also require the toolchain named in their briefs.

entryChecks.prompt: Implement a growable array in C. Force an allocation failure and show that the original contents remain owned and readable. Explain why returning a pointer to a local array is invalid.
entryChecks.criteria: A failed growth leaves the old pointer, length, capacity, and contents unchanged; successful growth transfers ownership exactly once. Tests cover empty input, growth, and failure. A local automatic array's lifetime ends on return, so its pointer cannot be used as a live object.

entryChecks.prompt: A buffer holds at most 8 items, with counters read and written initially zero. State an invariant, and construct one legal full-buffer state and one illegal state. Explain the extra assumption needed before these counters could be shared by threads.
entryChecks.criteria: For non-wrapping integer counters, 0 ≤ written − read ≤ 8. (read=3, written=11) is full; (3,12) violates capacity. Counter access and updates need a synchronization/atomicity contract; sequential arithmetic alone does not make a concurrent implementation safe.

entryChecks.prompt: For a 32-bit unsigned byte address, split address 0x1234 into a 4 KiB page number and offset. Then explain why a set of customer IDs and a list of customer IDs need not have the same size.
entryChecks.criteria: The page number is 1 and offset is 0x234 (564): 4096 + 564 = 4660. A list can repeat an ID while a set removes duplicates. If either argument is unfamiliar, repair binary arithmetic or set semantics before starting.

steps.title: Explain the machine
steps.outcome: Connect representation, instruction execution, memory traffic, and parallel performance in one falsifiable machine model.

gate.prompt: Defend the image-filter architecture against an altered workload. Submit your baseline and alternatives, then explain which observation would disprove your bottleneck claim.
criteria: Check accumulator width and boundary pixels against the specification.
Trace cache lines and DMA ownership rather than comparing instruction counts alone.
Separate computed ceilings from measurements; account for the latency tail and state unverified assumptions.

steps.title: Establish protected execution
steps.outcome: Trace authority, scheduling, memory, I/O, and recovery through a kernel change with reproducible tests.

gate.prompt: Submit the kernel capstone against its pinned source revision and rubric. Defend one invariant under a changed schedule and one injected failure.
criteria: Include reproducible build instructions, upstream and task-specific tests, and the exact revision.
Show an adversarial trace that distinguishes your implementation from a named incorrect version.
Explain liveness and failure boundaries. Simulation or a QEMU run is not a production-hardware measurement.

steps.title: Preserve application facts
steps.outcome: Express invariants as schema, transactions, and recovery behavior, then measure cost without sacrificing correctness.

gate.prompt: Build and defend the multi-tenant order-system capstone. Produce evidence under contention, retries, a crash, and one replication or migration failure.
criteria: Demonstrate tenant isolation, immutable accepted prices, and nonnegative inventory.
Test duplicate requests and explain which transaction owns each invariant.
Include query plans, reproducible workload measurements, and a recovery procedure with an explicit durability boundary.

synthesis.title: Trace one acknowledged order across the stack
synthesis.brief: Use your database capstone as the application and the OS/architecture models as explanatory tools, not as a claim that PostgreSQL runs on xv6. Choose one successful order acknowledgement. Trace the path from application state through kernel buffering to a declared durable storage boundary. Contrast a process crash, a machine power loss, and a retry after a lost response. State which failures your actual test environment can reproduce.
deliverables: An annotated sequence diagram identifying volatile and durable state, each acknowledgement, and the component responsible for each guarantee.
A prediction-and-observation matrix for the three failures. Include at least one deliberately incorrect variant and the test that detects it.
A workload comparison that separates CPU work, cache behavior, kernel waiting, and database I/O; label measured values and estimates separately.
A short defense responding to a reviewer who changes one assumption, such as storage flush guarantees or retry timing.
criteria: No unsupported leap from CPU store completion to power-loss durability.
No assertion of exactly-once effects without an explicit idempotency boundary and failure argument.
Tests distinguish the claimed guarantee from a plausible broken implementation; limitations remain visible.
An independent reviewer can reproduce the evidence and ask for revisions. Self-attestation is not certification.
synthesis.boundary: The 12-hour synthesis allowance is a planning estimate after the three course capstones, not a measured learner completion time. Preparation and external review time vary. This path does not teach production distributed consensus, hardware design sign-off, or a complete security specialization.
